text: That heartbeat shakes the whole cleft, and the walkway behind them shears off the rock and falls into the dark.
Stranded across the gap, the foreman decides this is above his pay grade and runs for the engineers.
What's left of the walkway tilts, and Jaeha hauls Uncle Pyo up as his bad knee buckles.
At the low end, a narrow ladder runs straight down into the dark.
Moon Ahin dusts off her coat. Jaeha sounds almost pleased: the only exit leads to Borro and Lyra.
For the first time, she looks at him properly, and offers a truce with an expiry date.
Jaeha holds out his hand to shake on it.
She walks straight past it.
Down the ladder they go, eighty metres, Moon Ahin first, Jaeha last.
At the bottom runs an ancient Far Side tunnel. Dami binds Jaeha's bleeding shoulder with her scarf.
Then Borro heaves out of the black water with Lyra on his shell, and the crew scream.
Lyra looks the heir up and down, slit to boots, and delivers a fashion verdict. The heir fires straight back.
Jaeha sweats between them. Nib chews dried squid and watches like it's a tennis match.
Each side sends a scout. Nib gets a partner he didn't ask for: her lead husk, Number One.
The goblin and the tall husk walk side by side, in silence.
They peek round the corner in exactly the same pose.
Further back, she asks why he still calls them husks after the stream. His answer is a trap-tester's: nobody steals something worthless.
He asks about her numbers. Her answer sounds learned by heart, from Uncle Taegun: what gets lost doesn't get a name.
Jaeha's rule runs the other way round: a name is how you keep something.
For one instant, her composure cracks.
Behind them, Ho finally asks the giant what he really is. Borro gives the only answer that matters.
Ho nods slowly, deeply impressed.
The scouts return: hounds ahead. Same news, different maths, and Nib's count is better.
Number One turns its blank face down at Nib. Somehow, it looks offended.
Ahead, in a round chamber, twelve eyeless ash hounds lap at light leaking from a cracked pipe, their alpha twice their size.
Jaeha sketches the fight: her husks hold the line, his summons strike, and the whole pack takes its cue from one howl.
She smells a trick: her husks do the dying, his take the credit. He insists nobody holds a line like hers.
Then Ho sneezes, and everyone freezes.
The alpha rises and howls, and twelve hounds snap upright.
Moon Ahin's baton drops, and thirty-seven husks slam into a wall, Borro's shield in the middle.
The pack hits it at once. Three husks crack, but the wall holds.
Jaeha throws all three summons into field form. Carry still covers only two at a time.
Nib drops into the pack from above, and Lyra rains arrows from a pipe cradle.
One arrow misses. Moon Ahin notices without even turning her head, and Lyra's pride takes the hit.
Then the alpha leaps the wall into the crew. Dami falls, and Uncle Pyo throws himself in front of her.
Jaeha has spotted the tell: the alpha freezes when it howls. Moon Ahin calls four numbers without a moment's doubt.
Four husks lock its legs. A fifth, number seventeen, takes its jaws and shatters.
The alpha howls, frozen for one instant, and Borro slams his shield into its chest.
Jaeha passes the blow through his body to Lyra, thirty percent lost on the way. His nose starts to bleed.
Borrowed Thunder. Her arrow leaves with the boom of Borro's blow behind it and punches clean through the alpha.
The rest of the pack flees whimpering.
Pyo is still shaking, arms spread in front of Dami. A decade of walking ahead for money, and only now for someone.
Moon Ahin kneels by the shattered husk and touches its broken face. It never had a name, only a silver seventeen.
Lyra spots the blood first. Jaeha waves it off and compliments her aim instead.
But Moon Ahin looks from the bloody glove to the bloody scarf, and understands where the wounds are going.
Across the broken husk, they explain themselves. Hers are perfect because they're empty. His aren't, so the pain has to go somewhere.
Deeper in, the air shimmers with heat, and the light turns deep violet.
Ho tries his theory again, smaller this time. Woo doesn't call him weird anymore.
The tunnel ends at a curved wall of glass thirty metres high. Behind the fog, a vast dark shape fills the space.
The fog clears for a moment on something rough and coral-red, then blooms white again, like breath on a window.
All three summons go tense, as if they recognize something.
Lyra, river-folk to the bone, goes pale. What she smells down here isn't river. It's salt.
Moon Ahin walks alone to a brass plate at the base of the frame.
Kanghan's hexagon, and under it, a small crescent moon: the Moon family's own mark.
Her baton sinks. The seal is her grandfather's, founder of the very division whose expenses brought her here.
Jaeha says it gently, because someone has to: her family put its name on whatever lives back there.
The vast shape is reflected in her eyes.
It breathes out, and the whole wall fogs white.
She presses a gloved hand to the glass and asks her question of a man who isn't there.
